claims.statement: Open SWE's PostgreSQL job queue persists one-shot and cron work by kind and payload; keyed scheduling replaces the existing keyed row by default, and cron jobs calculate their next fire in their configured timezone.

Workers claim due jobs with a lease and claim token so replicas do not concurrently execute a claimed job; they renew running claims, cancel a handler when its job is removed, and leave shutdown-interrupted work reclaimable after lease expiry.
Successful one-shot jobs are deleted while successful cron jobs advance and reset attempts; one-shot failures use bounded exponential retry and cron failures skip to the next fire.
Job startup migrates eligible legacy Agent Server crons under a claim, retains a cron when adoption fails, and installs standing thread-status reconciliation among other recurring jobs.

Schedule automations are stored with triggers and schedule triggers create keyed agent_schedule cron jobs; each cron fire is event-claimed by job ID and due time before launching to avoid duplicate launches after reclaim.

Automation delivery derives its only destination from the stored automation creator, rechecks authorization, and sends through that creator's linked Slack DM rather than trusting run-supplied routing.

The schedule_thread_wakeup tool accepts delays from one minute through 24 hours, persists a one-shot job with a system-identified input, and its handler creates an enqueued run with the completion webhook.

Thread wakeups are budgeted per human-message generation; the budget is recorded before scheduling, system wakeups do not reset it, and reclaimed or failed wakeup launches are deliberately not retried to avoid duplicate runs.

Background-command reconciliation supports runner callbacks or per-thread minute polling, tracks running task IDs in thread metadata, and delivers terminal completion back to the owner with an enqueued system agent run.

Background completion delivery uses a sandbox notify claim and notify.done marker to prevent callback and polling races from delivering twice, releases the claim after dispatch failure, and stops polling only after fresh idle verification.

Baby-sit watches persist their state on the pull request, use a keyed ten-minute job, associate the watch with the task coordinator thread, and prevent a separate task from concurrently watching the same PR.

A baby-sit evaluation serializes per-watch work with an event claim, classifies checks from GitHub check runs and commit statuses, waits for all required checks before ready, and wakes the owner thread through enqueued agent dispatches for ready or fixable failure states.

Baby-sit resets retry and deduplication state on a new head, deduplicates failure dispatches by head and retry count, caps flaky retries at three per head, and stops after bounded persistent evaluation or ready-dispatch errors.

The run-completion handler is fail-closed without RUN_COMPLETE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, refreshes thread status and settles turns, finalizes usage telemetry, and suppresses a user-facing reply for automated thread-wakeup failures.

Agent and Slack session costs are enriched asynchronously with five delayed attempts; agent cost is persisted and copied to per-invocation thread metadata, while session cost updates a mapped Slack response and clears its pending indicator when unavailable or exhausted.

The standing per-minute thread-status job reconciles stale busy threads and fails MDA runs silent for 90 minutes through normal completion handling before cancellation; a separate reconcile handler can interrupt pending LangGraph runs older than a configurable 30-minute default.
